evals.prompt: my mac is crawling and the fans are screaming — activity monitor shows like a dozen node processes all eating cpu and they're all from `node --test`. i'm not running any tests right now. can you find the dead ones and kill them without nuking my mcp servers or my editor?
evals.expected_output: Enumerates node processes (via pgrep, not ps -ax), identifies the leftover/runaway `node --test` ones (PPID==1 orphans and/or high-CPU-for-minutes runaways), shows them before killing, kills them with TERM then KILL, and explicitly leaves MCP servers / node_repl / editor node alone. Ideally uses or references the skill's reaper with a dry-run first.

evals.prompt: i just ran the unit suite and it said it finished but there are still a bunch of node --test processes hanging around afterward. clean them up, and i don't want this to keep happening every time i run tests.
evals.expected_output: Reaps the existing leftover `node --test` processes (cure), AND addresses recurrence: recommends/installs the prevention path (guarded runner + shell integration so future `node --test` runs can't leak, and/or the stop-hook). Distinguishes the one-time cleanup from the durable fix.

evals.prompt: run the node test suite for me but make sure it doesn't leave a pile of orphaned node processes behind this time like it did yesterday
evals.expected_output: Runs the tests through the guarded runner (guarded-test.sh) so the whole process group is torn down on exit regardless of pass/fail, rather than a bare `node --test`. Optionally reaps any pre-existing strays first. Confirms no leftovers remain after the run.
